description: Reads one graph you saved earlier, by its graph_id, or a graph another account shared with you, by its share_token, and returns the whole model in the same shape the run tools accept; an input saved without a distribution comes back with distribution_type null and distribution_params {}. Use this when you want to show the user what is in a saved model, or edit it before running it again: pass the edited model to run_monte_carlo_simulation as graph. To run a saved model unchanged, or with only a different trial count, you do not need this tool: call run_monte_carlo_simulation with its graph_id (and trials). To find a graph_id first, call list_graphs. It returns the graph_id, the name, when it was last updated, and the graph itself: its uncertain inputs with their distributions, the formula nodes, the links between them and the run settings with the metrics it asks for, plus its details and each node's unit and description, as saved, and the version number of what it returned. Pass version, a number from list_graph_versions, to read that earlier version instead of the current model: it comes back in the same shape, with the run settings and details it was saved with. Reading an earlier version changes nothing; to restore one, follow the steps in list_graph_versions. To read a model someone shared with you, pass share_token (the token they got from create_model_share_link, or a link containing it) instead of graph_id: it returns their model as currently saved, with graph_id null, and version cannot be used with it. You cannot change their model; run it by passing it to run_monte_carlo_simulation as graph, or keep your own copy with save_graph and no graph_id. It reads the model, not any result of running it. After a save_graph error nothing new was saved, so this returns the graph as it was before that call. It needs a Neumann account: send your key, or your signed-in token, in the Authorization header as a Bearer credential. No Neumann tool takes an api_key argument. Cost: free -- it debits no credits and spends none of your free daily runs -- but it needs an account; an anonymous caller gets account_required.

graph.description: The model itself, in the shape the run tools accept, except that an input saved without a distribution comes back with distribution_type null and distribution_params {}; such a graph cannot be run until you give that input a distribution. Each input comes back with its estimate (the range) beside its distribution_params; estimate.origin says whether the range was stated or worked out from the params. details, each node's unit and description, and run_params.output_request come back as they were saved; details is null when none was set. Edit it and pass it back to run_monte_carlo_simulation, or save the edited version with save_graph and this graph_id. Its full schema is run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph parameter.

graph_id.description: The id of the graph that was read; null when you read it with share_token, because the graph belongs to another account. To keep a copy, call save_graph without a graph_id.

version.description: The version number of the model returned: the one you asked for, or the latest when you did not ask for one. For an earlier version, updated_at is when that version was saved.
